metadata.title: Top US Finance News
metadata.ranking_basis: Rank 1 is the day's overall market close. After that, stories are ranked by how much they moved the market and how widely they were covered. The big-bank earnings that opened Q3 earnings season and the memory-chip selloff drove the day. They are followed by Fed rate-hike signals and yields, oil and diesel, other large-cap earnings, and housing data.
metadata.fact_check_method: Researched by web search, then every story was re-checked against its sources in a second pass; facts and stories the re-check could not support were removed.

verification_status_legend.verified: Key facts confirmed by a primary source or by two or more independent sources
verification_status_legend.partially_verified: Core event confirmed, but one or more specific figures rest on a single source or sources conflict

limitations: Compiled by the pipeline's news step by web search.

Some publisher pages blocked direct fetching (CNBC, AP via 10tv, TheStreet, Goldman Sachs' site, Inman, GlobeNewswire, Woodworking Network). For those, figures were checked against syndicated copies (AP via WTOP), SEC filings, or search-result excerpts. The CNBC Treasury-yield and CXMT pages were seen only as search excerpts.
Most closing share-price moves (Citi about 5.5%, the Memory ETF DRAM about 3.5%, Applied Materials more than 6.5%) come from a single Yahoo Finance market wrap. They are given as approximations.

AP rounds percent moves (Dow 0.3%, Nasdaq 0.2%). Search excerpts attributed to CNBC/Yahoo gave Dow -0.35% and Nasdaq -0.15%, but those pages could not be opened. Point changes and closing levels are from AP.
Oil: an early-morning Fortune snapshot (Brent $107.29 at 7:45 a.m. ET) and an Asia-session report (WTI $92.8) differ from the settlements. Only the Reuters settlement prices are used.
No NFIB small-business report or other major federal data release dated October 13, 2026 could be confirmed, so economic data is limited to NAR existing-home sales.
A Yahoo live blog quoted Broadcom CEO Hock Tan as saying many investors speculating on AI have 'no clue' what they are investing in. A second source could not be found, so it is left out.

stories.headline: Dow falls 180.45 points to 51,670.10 as bank earnings and a memory-chip selloff leave stocks nearly flat
stories.summary: US stocks ended slightly lower on Tuesday as investors weighed a large batch of big-bank and corporate earnings and a steep overnight drop in South Korean memory-chip stocks. The S&P 500 slipped 1.79 points to 7,805.45, just below its all-time high set the previous week. The Dow lost 180.45 points and the Nasdaq fell 41.52 points.
key_facts: S&P 500 fell 1.79 points, less than 0.1%, to 7,805.45
Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 180.45 points, or 0.3%, to 51,670.10
Nasdaq Composite fell 41.52 points, or 0.2%, to 27,204.38
Russell 2000 fell 11.11 points, or 0.4%, to 2,783.37
S&P 500 is up 14% for the year to date
Memory chip stocks fell for a second straight day

fact_check.notes: Closing levels and point changes are from the AP table syndicated by WTOP. The same Dow and S&P closing levels appeared in separate search excerpts attributed to CNBC/Yahoo. The direction of moves and the drivers (bank earnings, memory-chip weakness) match Yahoo Finance's market wrap.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Chase posts $15.3 billion third-quarter profit, up 6%, with earnings of $5.57 a share
stories.summary: JPMorgan Chase reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $15.3 billion, or $5.57 per diluted share, on managed revenue of $50.9 billion. Net interest income rose 13% to $27.1 billion. Results included a $658 million net loss on investment securities. Yahoo Finance said EPS fell short of an analyst forecast of $5.90, and the shares closed lower with the other big banks.
key_facts: Q3 2026 net income was $15.3 billion, up 6% year over year
Diluted EPS was $5.57
Managed revenue was $50.9 billion, up 8% year over year
Net interest income was $27.1 billion, up 13% year over year
Noninterest revenue was $23.8 billion, up 3%
Results included $658 million of net investment securities losses
Standardized CET1 capital ratio was 13.9%

fact_check.notes: Figures come from JPMorgan's 8-K filed October 13, 2026 (summarized by StockTitan) and match the TradingView headline. Yahoo Finance gave net revenue as $50.2 billion (a reported rather than managed basis), so the managed figure of $50.9 billion is used. The $5.90 analyst estimate rests on Yahoo Finance alone.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs earns $17.01 a share as equities trading revenue reaches $6.44 billion
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs reported third-quarter net revenues of $18.68 billion, 23% higher than a year earlier, and net earnings of $5.29 billion, or $17.01 per diluted share. Profit rose 29% from a year earlier, led by equities trading. Investment banking fees reached $3.22 billion. The stock rose more than 4% before the open but closed lower along with the other big banks.
key_facts: Q3 2026 net revenues were $18.68 billion, 23% higher than Q3 2025 and 8% lower than Q2 2026
Net earnings were $5.29 billion, or $17.01 per diluted share
Profit rose 29% year over year
Annualized return on equity was 18.7%
Equities net revenues were $6.44 billion
FICC net revenues were $3.47 billion
Investment banking fees were $3.22 billion

fact_check.notes: Figures were confirmed against Goldman's 8-K earnings release on SEC.gov. The 29% profit rise is from Yahoo Finance and BNN Bloomberg coverage. The premarket gain and lower close are from Yahoo Finance.

stories.headline: Chinese chipmaker CXMT's breakthrough claim sends Kospi down more than 5% and hits US memory stocks
stories.summary: China's CXMT said it will launch a data-center server memory chip using a 4F² cell design before the end of the year, a step ahead of Samsung and SK Hynix. South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5% as Samsung and SK Hynix tumbled. US memory names including Micron, Sandisk, Seagate and Western Digital fell for a second straight day. The claim has not been independently verified.
key_facts: CXMT said it will launch a data-center server chip with a 4F² design before year-end
South Korea's Kospi index fell more than 5%
Samsung is not expected to produce 4F² products until 2028
The Memory ETF (DRAM) fell roughly 3.5%
Applied Materials dropped more than 6.5%

fact_check.notes: The CXMT claim and the Kospi drop are confirmed by Yahoo Finance and a Gulf News/Bloomberg excerpt. Excerpts gave SK Hynix -10% and Samsung -7.4%, but those pages were not opened, so the figures are left out. The DRAM ETF (-3.5%) and Applied Materials (-6.5%) moves rest on the Yahoo Finance wrap alone.

stories.headline: Fed's Collins and Williams signal one more rate hike in 2026 as 10-year yield eases to about 5.22%
stories.summary: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said she expects it will be appropriate to raise rates a bit further before the end of the year to return inflation to 2%. New York Fed President John Williams told Bloomberg News that one more hike may be appropriate this year but he sees no reason for more in 2027. The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 2 basis points to roughly 5.22% as energy prices stabilized.
key_facts: Collins: it will be appropriate to 'raise rates a bit further before the end of the year'
Collins cited jumps in jet fuel, diesel and heating oil prices as pushing inflation above the 2% target in coming months
Williams: 'it may be appropriate to have one more rate hike' in 2026
Williams sees no reason at this time for further hikes in 2027
10-year Treasury yield fell about 2 basis points to about 5.22%

fact_check.notes: Collins' remarks are reported by Yahoo Finance and Bloomberg. Williams' remarks come from Reuters (via Investing.com/Yahoo) and Bloomberg. The 10-year yield is 5.22% per Yahoo Finance and 5.215% per a CNBC excerpt; the CNBC page could not be opened directly.

stories.headline: Brent settles down 96 cents at $105.69 while US diesel futures jump 5% despite Trump's Russia diesel deal
stories.summary: Oil prices settled mixed. Hopes that a US-Russia diesel deal would free up supply offset Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. President Trump said Russia agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel. US diesel futures still rose about 5% by midday to their highest in weeks as traders doubted the supply would arrive.
key_facts: Brent crude settled at $105.69 a barrel, down 96 cents, or 0.9%
WTI crude settled at $94.14 a barrel, up 40 cents, or 0.4%
US diesel futures rose about 5% by midday to their highest level in weeks
European diesel futures rose about 3.8%
NBC reported that the sanctions waiver on Russian fuel lasts until April 2027
National diesel prices are up 70% since February 28

fact_check.notes: Settlement prices are from Reuters (via Lufkin Daily News). The diesel futures jump is confirmed by both Reuters and NBC News. The April 2027 waiver date and the 70% rise in diesel prices rest on NBC News alone. Earlier intraday prices from other outlets (for example, WTI $94.45 at a Yahoo snapshot) differ from the settlements and are not used.

references.title: Oil prices settle mixed, focus on US-Russia diesel deal, Saudi Yemen attacks
Diesel futures jump, signaling higher prices to come despite Trump's Russia deal

stories.headline: Citigroup and Wells Fargo top profit forecasts, but Citi shares slide about 5.5%
stories.summary: Citigroup reported third-quarter net income of $5.2 billion, or $2.85 a share, on revenue of $23.8 billion, up 8% and its best third quarter in a decade. Wells Fargo earned $6.0 billion, or $1.87 a share, up 13%, on revenue of $21.87 billion. Wells Fargo's EPS beat estimates but its revenue missed. Citi had the steepest drop among the big banks, falling about 5.5%.
key_facts: Citi Q3 net income was $5.2 billion, or $2.85 per diluted share
Citi revenue was $23.8 billion, up 8%, the best third-quarter revenue in a decade
Citi RoTCE was 11.5%
Wells Fargo Q3 net income was $6.0 billion, or $1.87 per diluted share, with EPS up 13%
Wells Fargo revenue was $21.87 billion, up 2%
Wells Fargo ROTCE was 16.3%
Citi shares fell about 5.5%

fact_check.notes: Both banks' results are confirmed by their 8-K releases on SEC.gov. Citi's roughly 5.5% share decline rests on the Yahoo Finance wrap alone. Wells Fargo's revenue miss (estimate $22.31 billion) comes from a search excerpt and is not used as a figure.

stories.headline: Johnson & Johnson raises its outlook to $11.05–$11.15 a share, but stock falls nearly 6% on weak medtech
stories.summary: Johnson & Johnson reported third-quarter sales of $25.4 billion, up 5.9%, and adjusted EPS of $2.59. It raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $11.05–$11.15. MedTech sales grew only 2.5% operationally to $8.64 billion, and the shares fell nearly 6%.
key_facts: Q3 2026 sales were $25.4 billion, up 5.9%
Adjusted EPS was $2.59; reported EPS was $0.09
Innovative Medicine sales were $16.76 billion
MedTech sales were $8.64 billion, with 2.5% operational growth
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $11.05–$11.15 from $10.96–$11.11
Full-year sales guidance is $101.0–$101.4 billion
Shares fell nearly 6%

fact_check.notes: Financials are from J&J's 8-K exhibit on SEC.gov. The nearly 6% share decline is reported by both Yahoo Finance and GuruFocus.

stories.headline: UnitedHealth beats with $4.69 adjusted EPS and lifts its 2026 forecast to at least $20.50 a share
stories.summary: UnitedHealth Group reported third-quarter revenue of $112.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.69, well above an analyst estimate of $4.14. It raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to at least $20.50. The medical cost ratio improved to 88.4%. The shares rose before the open but ended slightly lower, according to Yahoo Finance.
key_facts: Q3 2026 revenue was $112.7 billion
EPS was $4.56; adjusted EPS was $4.69
Analysts expected adjusted EPS of $4.14
Medical cost ratio was 88.4%, versus 89.9% a year earlier
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook is at least $20.50; GAAP EPS outlook is at least $19.50
Earnings from operations were $6.6 billion

fact_check.notes: Revenue, EPS and outlook are from UnitedHealth's press release. The estimate and medical cost ratio comparison are from Yahoo Finance (Reuters). Moves before the open varied by source (2.5% to 4.3%). The slightly lower close rests on the Yahoo wrap alone.

stories.headline: Existing-home sales rise 1.5% in September to a 3.99 million annual rate
stories.summary: The National Association of Realtors said existing-home sales rose 1.5% in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million, down 2.2% from a year earlier. The median price rose 1.3% to $417,500. NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun said August and September were the two slowest months for home sales this year, as rising mortgage rates limit buyers.
key_facts: Sales rose 1.5% month over month to a 3.99 million annual rate
Sales were down 2.2% year over year
Median existing-home price was $417,500, up 1.3% year over year
Inventory was 1.60 million units, a 4.8-month supply
The 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.86%, up from 6.67% in August
First-time buyers were 31% of sales

fact_check.notes: The single reference is the primary source: the National Association of Realtors publishes the existing-home sales data itself. Its release, dated October 13, 2026, was opened again for this answer, and every figure above was rechecked against it: 3.99 million rate, +1.5% month over month, -2.2% year over year, $417,500 median (+1.3%), 1.60 million inventory, 4.8-month supply, 6.86% mortgage rate, 31% first-time buyers, and the Yun quote. A Woodworking Network story that appears to cover the same report could not be opened (HTTP 403), so it is not listed.

references.title: Existing-Home Sales Increased 1.5% in September, According to NAR Report
